rationale.intuition:
Regression lock for PR #267 anchor×0.1 floor: a very weak unhooked applicant at Harvard (GPA 3.2 / SAT 1300, no activities, no awards) should ALWAYS produce a probability below the pre-fix absolute floor of 2.0% AND above the new relative floor of anchor×0.1 (Harvard anchor=3.65% → floor=0.365%).

The range [0.2%, 1.8%] is *deliberately* set below 2.0% to assert the absolute floor of 0.02 is no longer in effect. If this fixture starts returning ≥ 2.0%, the absolute floor has been reintroduced — symptom of someone reverting prediction-counselor-fix or adding a Math.max(0.02, ...) clamp downstream.

The lower bound 0.2% is well below the relative floor (0.365%) to detect the opposite regression: if the relative floor was raised too high or the modifier product was capped, the prob would inflate above the floor.

sources.name: PR #267 — counselor floor anchor×0.1
sources.evidence: Replaced absolute floor Math.max(0.02, anchor*0.3) with relative floor anchor*0.1. Rationale (from counselor-engine.service.ts:270-280): old absolute floor flattened EVERY intl/weak profile at HYPSM-class schools to identical 2.0%, making predictions profile-blind.

sources.name: counselor-engine.service.ts (line 281)
sources.evidence: const lowerBound = anchor * 0.1; — engine source-of-truth for the floor formula. Harvard anchor=0.0365, floor=0.00365 (0.365%).

sources.name: Harvard CDS 2024-25 Section C9
sources.evidence: GPA 25th percentile ≈3.85; SAT 25th ≈1510. An applicant with 3.2 GPA / 1300 SAT is at the bottom 1% of the applicant pool — well below admit pool. Counselor consensus: <2% admit probability.

sources.name: NACAC State of College Admission 2024 §4.1
sources.evidence: HYPSM admits a small number of well-below-25th applicants each year (typically <5% of admit class) through hooks or extraordinary context. For an unhooked applicant with no hooks, the probability is genuinely below 2% but not zero.
